hints: Look at each statement separately, starting with what you know about the shape and bonding in ammonia.
Count the valence electrons around nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$ and think about what happens when $\text{NH}_3$ meets water to form $\text{OH}^-$.
Remember how ammonia gas is released in the lab from an ammonium salt, and ask whether you need an acid or a base to free it.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - bonding in ammonia**

Think of nitrogen with 5 outer electrons plus 3 hydrogens. That gives 3 N-H bond pairs and 1 lone pair left on nitrogen.

$$\text{N} : 2,5 \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 \text{ has 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, pyramidal}$$

**Check statement 2 - ammonia in water**

Ammonia is a base. It accepts a proton from water to make hydroxide ions.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$$
More $\text{OH}^-$ means higher pH, so bubbling $\text{NH}_3$ into neutral water increases pH above 7. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 - making ammonia gas**

To free $\text{NH}_3$ from $\text{NH}_4^+$, you need to remove $\text{H}^+$. That needs a base like $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, not an acid.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Warming ammonium sulfate with hydrochloric acid adds more $\text{H}^+$, so no $\text{NH}_3$ is released. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 are correct, statement 3 is incorrect. That matches the combination of 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. Warming an ammonium salt with an acid cannot produce ammonia, you need warming with a base to deprotonate NH4+.
options.B: Correct because statements 1 and 2 only are true. NH3 has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, and it forms OH- in water raising pH, while statement 3 is false.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3 and omits statement 1. Statement 1 is definitely true and statement 3 is definitely false.
options.D: Incorrect because it claims only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is also correct since aqueous ammonia is alkaline and increases pH.
